title: Learned morphology guides targeted isolation of gut bacteria
summary: A learned morphology model selected likely target genera for robotic isolation, followed by sequencing to confirm cultured organisms. This supports a bounded, experimentally tested recovery result. The platform's broader diversity-selection component uses feature distances and is not itself described as learned. Neither every isolate nor every genome is counted as a separate discovery, and clinical benefit was not established.

evidence.tested: New colonies selected by the taxonomy model were isolated and sequenced.
evidence.unknown: Generality beyond the studied samples and culture conditions remains unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: CAMII random-forest colony taxonomy prediction supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.

source_review.scope: Indexed primary publisher PDF targeted-isolation Methods, publisher abstract/date and affiliations; prior experimental Results review retained.
